$comment: The CATALOG. System-wide rules that hold for every tier-3 schema, stated once. A component schema references these by id instead of restating them; restating is what lets them drift. Each entry says which gate proves it, so an invariant with no gate is visibly unenforced rather than quietly aspirational.

gates.1: declared artefacts exist and are importable
gates.3: cross-layer coherence (CSS × core TS × bindings × docs)
gates.5: visual, across the four dimensions + forced-colors (CDP)

invariants.statement: Every color-valued hook resolves to a tier-2 semantic token: never a --ramp-*, never a literal color.
invariants.why: A hook reaching into a ramp bypasses the mode layer and breaks dark mode for that component alone.

invariants.statement: A variant, size or state rule never introduces a hook name absent from the base set.
invariants.why: Both hook idioms satisfy this and it is the rule that keeps them from multiplying. A `redeclare` group reassigns a base hook (--sk-button-bg per variant); a `read` group assigns a property that reads a base hook (--sk-tabs-trigger-selected-fg under [data-selected]). Either way the base declares every name, which is what stops one hook per combination.

invariants.statement: Every rule sits inside @layer components; nothing targets :root.
invariants.why: An unlayered rule beats any layered one regardless of specificity, so it removes the consumer's override surface.

invariants.statement: No hover, press, focus or selected color is declared here. Interaction paint is the state-layer pattern's, always.
invariants.why: Per-component interaction colors are exactly the one-color-per-combination explosion the state layer exists to delete (ADR-9).

invariants.statement: A selector keys off exactly one axis unless its exact selector is listed in couplings.
invariants.why: Axes compose in the cascade; listing the rare coupling keeps combinations explicit and reviewable.

invariants.statement: The first value of each axis is the base default and carries no selector; every later value carries exactly one.
invariants.why: A default with its own rule is a value that can disagree with the base. A non-default without one is a value that silently does nothing.

invariants.statement: Every base or group color that needs a forced-colors override has one inside @media (forced-colors: active).
invariants.why: In forced colors the system repaints backgrounds and borders; a variant left out becomes an invisible or unreadable control.

invariants.statement: A components/ sheet paints structure on import, or composes another component's hooks.
A components/ sheet declares at least one --sk-* hook, so it has a public restyle surface.
Declared custom-property names are lowercase kebab.
Every axis value exists in all declared surfaces: the CSS rule, the core TS union, every binding, and a docs example.
invariants.why: This is the failure mode a generator produces most: a value added to the CSS and not to the type, or to the type and not to the docs.

invariants.statement: Every declared part exists as a class in the CSS and as a key in the core parts object.
Every host element has a binding, behaviour tests and a docs example of its own.
invariants.why: A second host is a second public surface. Undocumented hosts are how <a class="sk-button"> got used three times with no contract.

invariants.statement: Every class listed in requires is verified at runtime by the binding that owns the markup contract.
invariants.why: A required companion that nothing checks is a silent dependency; it fails as a subtle layout bug far from its cause.

invariants.statement: Every binding derived from id is reachable by bare specifier through its package's exports map.
invariants.why: The docs teach bare specifiers; a file not in the map does not exist for a consumer.

invariants.statement: The enhancer patches attributes on elements that already exist. It renders no markup and writes no class.
Mounting twice enhances zero elements the second time.
When the markup contract is broken the enhancer fails loudly, with the fix in the message.
A control with no visible text carries an authored accessible name, and the binding refuses one without it.
Glyphs are aria-hidden and never contribute to the accessible name.
Component state is exposed to assistive technology, not only painted.
The interactive area measures at least --size-touch-target on both axes, whatever size the face paints.
The component stays legible and its states stay distinguishable under forced-colors.
State is written by the machine as a data attribute, never as a BEM modifier and never toggled by hand.
Part class names are ours and permanent: they survive replacing the machine underneath.
invariants.why: Which is why parts are named in BEM rather than in the machine's vocabulary.
